Reconstructed Niño3.4 ENSO index, 1301–2005 (Li et al. 2013)

Source: R/data.R
enso_nino34.Rd

Annual reconstruction of the El Niño/Southern Oscillation from 2,222 tree-ring chronologies across Asia, New Zealand and the Americas. Each value is the November–January Niño3.4 sea-surface temperature anomaly of the winter that ends in January of year. A global covariate on a yearly clock: it takes one value at each time for every dyad, so its effect on a relational event process is identified only through time-shifted case-control sampling, sample_non_events() with shift = "exponential".

Usage

enso_nino34

Format

A data frame with 705 rows and 2 columns:

year

Integer year CE, 1301–2005.

nino34

Reconstructed November–January Niño3.4 sea-surface temperature anomaly (°C), relative to the 1971–2000 observed mean. The file gives no uncertainty for the reconstruction.

Source

NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information, World Data Service for Paleoclimatology, study 14632, https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/access/paleo-search/study/14632, doi:10.25921/jfqm-9178 ; file enso-li2013.txt, accessed 2026-10-16. NCEI states that all data products of its Paleoclimatology Product Area are publicly available without restriction.

Details

To use it as a piecewise-constant covariate in simulate_relational_events(), pass data.frame(time_start = enso_nino34$year, nino34 = enso_nino34$nino34) as global_covariates, which holds each winter's value through the calendar year that it opens. For event data after 1950, NOAA's instrumental Oceanic Niño Index (monthly) is the better covariate. The raw file is shipped as system.file("extdata", "enso_nino34", "enso-li2013.txt", package = "amorem"); data-raw/enso_nino34.R in the source repository rebuilds this object.

References

Li J, Xie S-P, Cook ER, Morales MS, Christie DA, Johnson NC, Chen F, D'Arrigo R, Fowler AM, Gou X, Fang K (2013). El Niño modulations over the past seven centuries. Nature Climate Change 3, 822–826. doi:10.1038/nclimate1936 .

Examples

data(enso_nino34)
plot(enso_nino34$year, enso_nino34$nino34, type = "l",
     xlab = "year", ylab = "Niño3.4 anomaly (°C)")
